groups.title: Laravel Routing Internals
groups.question: Your Laravel routes load models by hand and build URLs as hard-coded strings. Explain how route model binding and named routes clean this up.

followUps.Route Model Binding: How does route model binding work and what happens when the model does not exist?
followUps.Named Routes and URL Generation: Why use named routes instead of hard-coded URLs?

evidence.text: Laravel loads the model automatically from the route parameter.
It matches the parameter name to the type-hinted model and its key.
If no record is found, Laravel returns a 404 automatically.

notEnough: Only saying Laravel injects the model.

evidence.text: Routes are given names and URLs are generated from them.
Changing a path updates every generated link automatically.
Hard-coded URLs break silently when paths change.

notEnough: Only saying routes can have names.

groups.title: Middleware Pipeline
groups.question: Admin routes need authentication, logging and a URL prefix, and a teammate is confused about why some middleware code runs after the response is built. Explain Laravel's middleware.

followUps.How Middleware Wraps the Request Lifecyc: How can middleware run code both before and after the controller?
followUps.Route Groups and Middleware Inheritance: How do route groups help with shared middleware and prefixes?

evidence.text: Each middleware wraps the next layer like an onion.
Code before calling the next layer runs on the way in.
Code after it runs on the way out, with the response available.
A group applies middleware, prefixes and names to many routes at once.
Every route in the group inherits those settings.
This avoids repeating them and forgetting one on a new route.

groups.title: Artisan CLI
groups.question: You keep creating controllers by hand with typos in namespaces, and a nightly cleanup task runs from a random script. Explain how Artisan helps.

followUps.Artisan Make Commands and Code Generatio: What do Artisan's make commands give you?
followUps.Custom Artisan Commands for Automation: Why turn a recurring task into a custom Artisan command?

evidence.text: make commands create files like controllers, models and migrations.
Generated files follow Laravel's naming and namespace conventions.
This avoids small mistakes from writing boilerplate by hand.
A custom command wraps an operational task in a named CLI tool.
It can be run in any environment the same way.
It can be scheduled by Laravel's scheduler.

notEnough: Only saying you can create commands.

groups.title: Service Container Basics
groups.question: A controller creates its own mailer and payment client with new, and tests cannot replace them. Explain how Laravel's service container and facades work.

followUps.Automatic Constructor Injection: How does Laravel inject dependencies into a controller's constructor?
followUps.Facades vs. Dependency Injection: What is a facade, and why might you prefer constructor injection?

evidence.text: The container reads the constructor's type hints.
It creates and passes in the needed objects automatically.
Because they come from the container, tests can replace them with fakes.
A facade is a static-looking proxy to an object in the container.
It hides the dependency, so a class's needs are not visible in its constructor.
Constructor injection makes dependencies explicit and easier to test, though facades can also be faked.
